name: Folliculotropic Mycosis Fungoides

criteria.description: Presence of atypical lymphocytic infiltrate centered on hair follicles with folliculotropism on skin biopsy
Clinical presentation with follicular papules, plaques, or acneiform lesions predominantly on head and neck
Immunophenotypic evidence of T-cell clonality with CD4+ predominance and loss of pan-T-cell markers
Detection of T-cell receptor gene rearrangement confirming monoclonality
Exclusion of other cutaneous lymphomas and inflammatory folliculitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological evidence of folliculotropic atypical lymphocytes plus compatible clinical presentation and immunophenotyping
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, and immunophenotypic data.

searchTerms: abnormal lymphocyte infiltration around hair follicles
atypical immune cells in follicular skin areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Follicular papules and plaques localized to head and neck
searchTerms: small raised bumps and plaques on head and neck
follicular papules localized to scalp and neck
clustered skin bumps on head and neck
acne-like skin lesions with prominent follicles

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Patchy alopecia in involved scalp regions

searchTerms: red plaques with visible hair follicles
skin patches lighter or darker than normal
areas of skin color loss or darkening

occasional.symptomName: Cystic lesions or comedones in follicular areas
searchTerms: cyst-like bumps or blackheads in follicular areas

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

occasional.symptomName: Erosions or ulcerations in advanced lesions
searchTerms: skin erosions or open sores in advanced lesions
damaged skin with breaks or ulcers

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (weight loss, night sweats)
searchTerms: systemic symptoms like chills and weight loss
B symptoms including sweating and fever

rare.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy due to nerve infiltration

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear usually normal; occasional Sézary cells in advanced disease
imaging: CT or PET scans may show lymphadenopathy or extracutaneous involvement
genetic: T-cell receptor gene rearrangement demonstrating monoclonality
other: Skin biopsy with immunohistochemistry showing CD3+, CD4+ atypical T-cells with loss of CD7

distinguishingFeatures: Epidermotropic rather than folliculotropic lymphocytic infiltrate
More widespread patches and plaques without follicular prominence
Lack of atypical lymphocytes on biopsy
Neutrophilic infiltrate rather than atypical lymphocytes
Usually infectious etiology with acute onset

redFlags: Rapidly progressive skin plaques with ulceration
Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats)
Neurological deficits suggestive of nerve infiltration
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
